WITH first_baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(pulsepersec) as baseline_1
  FROM signals
  WHERE pulsepersec IS NOT NULL
),
telescope_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    telescref,
    AVG(pulsepersec) as avg_pulse_rate
  FROM signals
  WHERE pulsepersec IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY telescref
),
above_first_baseline AS (
  SELECT 
    ta.telescref,
    ta.avg_pulse_rate
  FROM telescope_averages ta
  CROSS JOIN first_baseline fb
  WHERE ta.avg_pulse_rate > fb.baseline_1
),
second_baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pulse_rate) as baseline_2
  FROM above_first_baseline
),
final_telescopes AS (
  SELECT 
    afb.telescref,
    afb.avg_pulse_rate
  FROM above_first_baseline afb
  CROSS JOIN second_baseline sb
  WHERE afb.avg_pulse_rate > sb.baseline_2
)
SELECT 
  AVG(ft.avg_pulse_rate) as mean_avg_pulse_rates,
  AVG(ft.avg_pulse_rate - (SELECT baseline_1 FROM first_baseline)) as mean_exceeds_first_baseline,
  AVG(ft.avg_pulse_rate - (SELECT baseline_2 FROM second_baseline)) as mean_exceeds_second_baseline
FROM final_telescopes ft

assumptions.assumption: Missing values in pulsepersec are represented as NULL and should be excluded from all AVG() calculations
The word 'above' in 'average is above this baseline' means strictly greater than (>) rather than >= (i.e., averages equal to a baseline are not kept)

alternatives.interpretation: If 'above' should be interpreted as greater-than-or-equal-to (>=), use >= instead of > in both WHERE clauses of the above_first_baseline and final_telescopes CTEs
